findings.evidence: Its three fields are `vertexIdempotent_mul_self` (PathAlgebra.lean:565), `vertexIdempotent_mul_vertexIdempotent_of_ne` (PathAlgebra.lean:558) and `one_def` (PathAlgebra.lean:591) — all in PathAlgebra.lean, whose module docstring already advertises exactly this cluster ('the vertex idempotents sum to `1`; they are orthogonal by ..., idempotent by ...'). The roadmap likewise lists the vertex idempotents with `∑ᵥ eᵥ = 1` as part of the path-algebra construction (QuiverRepresentations/README.md:213), not the module step.
findings.fix: Move the theorem into `TauCeti/RepresentationTheory/Quiver/PathAlgebra.lean` next to `one_def` (line 591), adding `public import Mathlib.RingTheory.Idempotents` there; `ModuleDecomposition.lean` then just applies it. PathAlgebra.lean is 898 lines against the 1500 ceiling, so there is room.
findings.issue: `completeOrthogonalIdempotents_vertexIdempotent` is an algebra-level statement about `kQ` with no module theory in it — it needs only `[Semiring k] [Fintype Q]`, strictly weaker than the `CommSemiring`/`Field` + `Module (pathAlgebra k Q) M` context of every other section here. It is the bundled form of three lemmas that all live in the earlier `PathAlgebra.lean`, so a consumer wanting the complete orthogonal family (e.g. `Quiver/PrimitiveIdempotent.lean`, whose docstring already calls `1 = ∑ᵥ eᵥ` 'the input to the primitive-idempotent decomposition', or `Quiver/Radical.lean`) must import the whole module-decomposition stack to get it.

summary: The generic/specific file split and all imports are correct, but the pure path-algebra fact `completeOrthogonalIdempotents_vertexIdempotent` is stranded in the module-decomposition file instead of `PathAlgebra.lean`, where the three lemmas it bundles already live.
